faq: How do you decide what a best seller is?
We use your recent orders, usually the last 30 or 90 days, and exclude items that are out of stock or low margin if you ask. We show you the rule so it is easy to change.
What counts as a new visitor?
Someone with no earlier visits recognized by your store. We use only on site data and follow your cookie settings, so someone who declines cookies is treated as new.
Can the rules differ by traffic source?
Yes, on Standard and Premium. For example, visitors from a gift guide see gifts first, while visitors from search see best sellers. We need to know the source tags you already use.

desc:
New visitor product rules decide what a first time shopper sees when your store knows nothing about them. Ecom Swift LLC sets clear rules for best sellers, new arrivals and top rated items, then places them where newcomers actually look.

## The first visit problem

A returning customer leaves a trail of views and orders. A first time visitor leaves nothing, so a suggestion tool has no signal to work with. Many stores respond by showing a random mix or an empty block, and the visitor lands on a page that feels generic.

The first visit decides whether someone stays long enough to learn what you sell. Showing proven products in a clear order gives newcomers a quick way in, even before the store knows their taste.

## What are new visitor rules?

New visitor rules are simple instructions that tell your store which products to show to people who have no browsing history. For example: show the most ordered items, hide anything out of stock, and add a row of new arrivals. The rules apply until the store has enough data to personalize.

## How first impressions affect results

Newcomers behave differently from regulars. They compare, they look for proof and they want a short path to something that fits. A best sellers row acts as social proof without any claims: these are the items other people actually buy.

Rules by traffic source go one step further. A visitor from a gift guide article and a visitor from a search ad arrive with different intent. Showing each group a fitting first row can make the page feel relevant straight away. Results depend on your catalog and traffic, so the higher packages include a test of one rule.

## What a good set of first visit rules includes

- A written definition of best seller for your store, such as orders in a set period.
- Out of stock and hidden products excluded.
- A new arrivals section for fresh products.
- A top rated section when you have product reviews.
- Placement on the home page and on key collection pages.
- Different rules by traffic source, such as social, search or email.
- A seasonal rule that you can switch on and off.
- A clean switch to returning visitor sections once data exists.
- A check of mobile layout and page speed.

## How we set it up

We start by agreeing what best seller means. Revenue, units and recent orders can give different lists, so we compare them and choose one that suits your range. We also decide how often the list refreshes.

Then we build the sections in your theme, apply your design and set the rules for visibility. We define what counts as a new visitor in your tool and test the page with a fresh browser profile and again as a returning visitor, to confirm the switch works.

The Basic package covers a best sellers section on the home page. Standard adds a new arrivals section, rules by traffic source and collection page placement. Premium adds top rated products, a seasonal rule, a clean handover to returning visitor sections, an A and B test of one rule and a short report.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Define best seller in writing.
- Keep each section short and focused.
- Hide products that cannot be bought.
- Match the first row to where visitors come from.
- Revisit the rules when your range changes.

**Avoid:**
- Showing the same row to every visitor forever.
- Using a best seller list built on old data.
- Mixing several themes in one row.
- Adding many sections to the home page.
- Treating this as a replacement for later personalization.

## Who this is for

This service suits new stores with little traffic history, stores that run paid ads to cold audiences and stores that are about to add personalization. It also suits owners whose home page shows only a banner and nothing a newcomer can buy straight away.

## What we need from you

Tell us which products you want to lead with and any you want to keep out of the rule. Share your main traffic sources and a sentence on what a new visitor usually wants. Access as a collaborator, staff or developer user is enough, and we never need your password.
